Built as 6 parts + 30 gable dormers: gross face areas equal the Bramac faces (existing roof 161.93 m² both), lines within 2.4% (valleys 0.1%). Area is 4.7% under Bramac because Bramac deducts less under each dormer (3.46 m² against the geometric 4.57 m²) and counts roof under the existing roof's overhang, which the core hides (cross gables, 12° shed).

4.note: A = tiles (priced), B = standing-seam metal (not priced). The metal decks are wide shed dormers cut into the tiled roof; their eave height is set so they meet the roof at the drawn depth (3.84 m in object A, 3.174 m in object B, from section B-B). Object B's eave height is 10.1 m, from the ridge and the 45° pitch; the +10.0 label is the cornice. Its east deck starts at the junction of the two wings. Object A: tiles 110.4 m² against 113 (-2.3%); the deck labels hint at a depth of 4.0-4.25 m against the drawn 3.84 m, unresolved. Object B: two wings (the oblique one as its own part), 11 decks; tiles 459.4 m² against 455 (+1.0%), ridge 75.8 m against the ridge tiles' 75.7-77.1 m.

2.note: raster at about 113 dpi; the only sheet is the truss plan, no section. The 41° hip roof matches (147.9 m² against 150) and alone accounts for the ridge tiles (ridge + hips 34.4 m against 34.3-35.7). The 12° roofs come out 101.7 m² against 110 (-7.6%) whether they are built as sheds or low gables (same footprint, same pitch), so the gap is in their footprint or overhang, not their form. The truss plan's symmetric purlins around a central purlin on a steel column hint at a low gable on the west wing, but a gable adds 7-17 m of ridge the offer has no ridge tiles for. The offer's verge (41-45 m) and valley (16-20 m) pieces fit neither form. Needs the section.
